Stanford CME295 names position bias and the swap-and-majority remedy (8fNP4N46RRo@23, @24); the Northeastern lecture gives the 'always favors the first or the second' framing and training-time shuffling (N_DwZR--XCc@46); the RAG-metrics talk gives randomised order and allowing ties as pairwise best practice (cRz0BWkuwHg@6); and the evals playbook gives the paired swap test, the 'neither answer has demonstrated superiority' reading of a flip, the aggregate-or-report-reversals production rule and anonymised pairs (PjCwlX0XT8o@36, @37, @32). Added as a new lever card directly after the pairwise card, with a cited pointer sentence in the pairwise card itself so the correction lands where the reader was reading.

reason: Added a full diagram section with five inline-SVG architectural drawings covering exactly what was asked: an agent architecture with every place a judge can be attached (input, retrieval, tool calls, output, trajectory, agent-as-judge), the parallel-vs-inline-vs-post-hoc topology, plus the other parts of the write-up that are genuinely diagrammable (instrument ladder, calibration loops, confusion matrix). The /lavish whiteboard skill is not available on this run, so the drawings are hand-authored SVG in that style — monochrome currentColor strokes, dashed boxes for judges, no external scripts, works in light and dark. One part of the request could not be honoured from the corpus: no talk presents a reference architecture, a per-turn judge-call budget, or a rule for combining J1-J7 into one release decision, so that is recorded as a caveat (architecture-p2) and a new gap (gaps-li11) instead of being drawn from memory.
